nd scene statistics.
﻿# dsh-preview-blender
Preview Blender **`.blend`** files inside DeepSeek Harness: the right-Sidebar document preview turns
the scene into an interactive 3D viewport (orbit / zoom / wireframe) with a scene-information panel
, instead of the built-in “binary file, no preview” empty state.
## What it does
- Registers a document-preview renderer for `.blend` files, so clicking one in **Workspace files** o

pens it in the right Sidebar.
- Runs `blender --background` once per file version to export a **GLB*
* plus a scene JSON (objects, triangles, materials, real-world size in mm, units, cameras, lights, c

ollections).
- Draws the GLB with a small **dependency-free WebGL viewer** written for this plugin:
orbit, pan, wheel zoom, double-click reset, wireframe mode, auto-rotate, a soft contact shadow and a

n axis triad. No CDN, no three.js.
- Caches conversions under `~/.dsh/cache/preview-blender`; the se

cond open is instant (a few milliseconds).
- Shows the scene facts that matter for CAD/3D-printing w
ork: per-object triangle counts and bounding-box sizes in millimetres, material swatches, scene unit
k: per-object triangle counts and bounding-box sizes in millimetres, material swatches, scene units.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness 0.2.x (declared compatible with `0.2.0-rc.2` and `0.2.1-rc.2`).
- **Blender 3.6 /
4.x / 5.x** installed. The plugin auto-detects `DSH_BLENDER`, `BLENDER_PATH`, `blender` on `PATH`,
the Steam library, and `C:\Program Files\Blender Foundation\Blender*`. Set `blenderPath` if your ins

tall lives elsewhere.
- A browser/GPU with WebGL (the DSH desktop app always has it).
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The package ships a `cordis.patch.yml`, so installation adds the plugin row automatically. Restart D
SH after installing.
## Configuration
Settings → Plugins → **Blender preview** (namespace `preview-blender`):
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `enabled` | `true` | Register the renderer and the conversion route. |
| `routePath` | `/api/previ
ew/blender` | Authenticated conversion route. Must stay under `/api`; otherwise the authenticated fe

nce is bypassed, so it falls back to the default. |
| `extensions` | `["blend"]` | Suffixes that ope

n in the 3D preview. |
| `blenderPath` | `""` (auto) | Absolute path of `blender.exe` / `blender`. |
| `cacheDir` | `""` → `~/.dsh/cache/preview-blender` | Where exported GLB files and scene JSON live

. |
| `timeoutMs` | `180000` | Wall-clock ceiling for one cold conversion. |
| `maxBytes` | `1073741

824` | Largest `.blend` converted (1 GiB). |
| `applyModifiers` | `true` | Apply modifiers during ex

port, so the preview matches what Blender renders. |
| `cacheEntries` | `24` | Cached conversions ke
pt on disk before the oldest are pruned. |
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- `lib/scene.py` exports with `export_apply`, `use_visible`, **Y-up**, no cameras/lights, and writes
the scene description (world-space AABBs through the evaluated depsgraph, Principled base colours c

onverted to sRGB swatches).
- The route lives under `/api`, so the connection service authenticates

every request (Host/Origin fence + session cookie). Arbitrary local files are not exposed.
- The vie
wer is a hand-written glTF 2.0 subset renderer (POSITION + NORMAL, indexed triangles, PBR factors, n
ode TRS/matrix). Textures, skinning and animation are out of scope; the Host only exports still scen
TRS/matrix). Textures, skinning and animation are out of scope; the Host only exports still scenes.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`lib/client.js` is generated — edit the files under `dev/` and rebuild. The DSH client loader hands
the bundle a `require` limited to the platform seed modules, so the package cannot pull a renderer d
ependency at runtime; the single generated file is the intended shape.
## Notes and limits
- A cold conversion takes roughly 2–10 s for a small scene (Blender startup dominates); it is cached

per file version, so rotating/zooming never re-runs Blender.
- Very large scenes (millions of trian

gles) export slowly and may exceed `timeoutMs`.
- Textures are not shown in the viewport (base colou

rs only); the Blender renders next to the file are still the reference.
- Nothing is uploaded: Blend
er runs locally and the GLB stays in the local cache.
